To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the electrochemical insertion of zinc ions into KNF 086 in organic electrolytes was demonstrated for the first time, and the electrochemical inter-calation of zinc ions in KNF 086 was investigated by X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) analysis and first-principles density functional theory (DFT) calculations.
an organic electrolyte-based rechargeable zinc ion (ZIB) battery was demonstrated using a Prussian blue (NB) analogue potassium nickel cyanoferrate (KNF 86) as the cathodic material.
we have developed a rechargeable zinc ion cell with an organic electrolyte, using a potassium nickel hexacyannoferrate cathode.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new type of organic electrolyte based Zn-ion batteries using Prussian blue analogue as the cathode.
a novel approach to the synthesis of Prussian blue (Fe 3 [Fe(CN)6]3) analogues with the aim of developing new materials for electrochemical applications.
the synthesis of Prussian blue analogue potassium nickel hexacynaferrate (KNF) and the electrochemical insertion and removal of zinc ions into and from the KNF lattice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
an organic electrolyte system based on a Prussian blue analogue is an effective way to achieve high performance rechargeable ZIBs with a high cycling efficiency.
the zinc ion insertion into KNF 086 occurs via an interstitial site in the cubic PB framework, and the electrochemical zinc insertion reaction is reversible in the organic electrolyte system.
an organic electrolyte system based ZIB using a KNF 86 as cathode material has been successfully demonstrated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the organic electrolyte based Zn ion battery is a promising energy storage system for future applications, and that the electrochemical inter-calation chemistry of Zn ions in the organic electrolyte system is a crucial factor for developing the Zn ion battery.
the organic solvent electrolyte based ZNBs have been successfully demonstrated and the intercalation chemistry for zinc in the PB analogue has been clarified.
this study provides a new perspective on organic electrolyte based zinc ion batteries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
organic electrolyte based zinc ion batteries can be used to store zinc ions.
the organic solvent system can be used as an electrolyte for zinc ion batteries.
the organic electrolyte system is more suitable for rechargeable Zn ion batteries than the aqueous electrolyte system.
